title: Uniform proper heart bound on the constructible weak Serre coproduct closure over a qcqs base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, and a finite commutative ring $A$ annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda$ be one of $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$: $A$ is discrete and the other rings have their induced $\ell$-adic topologies, as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, and let $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ be proper morphisms. For $T=X,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$, with ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A_T)$ and total right derived module-object pushforward $Rf_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Use the small-site and indexing universe of [def-weil-size-convention].
Let $\mathcal P_X$ be the intersection of all classes of objects of $\mathcal A_X$ which contain zero and every constructible module in the finite constant scalar-model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and are closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between members, extensions, and all small coproducts computed in $\mathcal A_X$. Here extension closure means that the middle object of a short exact sequence belongs to the class whenever both end objects do. There is an integer $d\geq0$, independent of $M$, such that
$$H^r(Rf_*(M[0]))=0\qquad(M\in\mathcal P_X,\ r>d).$$
The symbol $M[0]$ denotes the complex concentrated in degree zero. The statement concerns only such heart objects. No assumption of derived completeness, invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes, existence of a field of definition, Noetherianity, or finite dimension of $S$ is made.

proof.text: Properness makes Y and X qcqs. The finite-type fibre-dimension theorem provides e bounding all ordinary fibres of f. For a morphism Spec K → Y, factor through the residue field of its image point and use the field-base-change dimension upper bound. Pullback associativity therefore bounds every geometric fibre of every base change by e. Set d = 2e + 2.

proof.text: On qcqs schemes finite constant-model constructibility is finite constant stratified constructibility. Use the proved stratified_pullback helper in the Zariski-locality module to pull back these generators. Exact pullback and its coproduct-preserving adjunction imply that the inverse image of the target weak Serre coproduct class has all the defining closure properties, so minimality gives pullback preservation of the entire heart class.

proof.text: Fix a heart object M and an affine w-contractible test Spec R → Y. Proper closed-fibre rigidity supplies the closed-point scheme C = Spec(R/Jac(0)), its affineness, reducedness, zero-dimensionality, w-contractibility and separably closed residue fields, and an isomorphism from derived evaluation on X ×_Y Spec R to derived sections on X_C of a^*M. Transport the ring properties through Γ(Spec(R/Jac(0))) ≅ R/Jac(0).

proof.text: The map X_C → C is proper. Pullback associativity identifies its geometric fibres with geometric fibres of f, so the bound e from Step 1 applies. The profinite geometric-family estimate and Step 2 show that the derived sections of a^*M have zero cohomology for r > 2e + 2. Transfer this vanishing through the rigidity isomorphism.

proof.text: Abelian evaluation on an affine w-contractible test is exact, as is forgetting the internal module action; therefore the composite evaluation is exact. Underived evaluation after f_* is evaluation at X ×_Y Spec R, with the fibre-product symmetry identifying the two conventions for pullback order. The existing exact-functor right-derived composition and homology comparison isomorphisms give evaluated H^r(Rf_*M[0]) ≅ H^r of derived evaluation. Thus Step 4 gives zero on every such test. The w-contractible covering basis and sheaf separatedness make every section zero; the faithful module forgetful functor then detects the zero module.
